love.up: The Fool suggests meeting someone or something new without a script. If you are single, it leans towards saying yes to an unplanned invitation and letting curiosity lead. In a relationship, it points to a fresh, playful step together, taken lightly and honestly.
love.rev: Reversed, the Fool points to hesitating at the cliff edge or leaping without looking. Single, you may be avoiding openness or chasing a rush. In a relationship, it suggests pausing to talk about what each of you actually expects before the next big step.

career.up: A new project, course or change of direction may be calling, and the Fool leans towards starting before you feel qualified. Travel light and accept being a beginner. For money, it suggests small, curious experiments rather than one big bet.
career.rev: Reversed, the Fool suggests either stalling at the edge of a decision or jumping in with no plan. Check the ground first: gather the basics, read the terms, ask someone who has done it. Money choices deserve extra care and a little patience now.

feelings.up: The other person may feel drawn to you with open, almost boyish enthusiasm. They are curious, a little nervous, and perhaps unsure how to say it. Their feelings seem light and sincere, though not yet carefully thought through.
feelings.rev: The other person may be unsure of their own feelings, or acting on impulse without thinking of the consequences. Interest could be real but scattered, or held back by fear of making it real. Their behaviour may not match their words yet.

yesno.up: Yes. The Fool leans towards going ahead, with trust and a light pack. Expect to be clumsy at first, and keep your eyes open as you step.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The Fool reversed suggests you are either holding back or rushing. Look at the ground before you decide, then the answer may become clearer.

advice.up: Take the first step, even if it is small. Travel light, keep your sense of humour, and let yourself be a beginner. Trust your instinct, as the little dog at your heel does.
advice.rev: Pause and check the ground before you move. If you have been preparing forever, choose one small action today. If you have been rushing, slow down and tell someone your plan.

love.up: The Magician suggests that you already have what you need to build connection: attention, honesty and a willingness to act. If single, show up and say what you want. In a relationship, it points to making your intentions visible through small, deliberate gestures.
love.rev: Reversed, the Magician points to charm without sincerity, or to feelings you know but have not voiced. Single, you may be performing rather than being yourself. In a relationship, it suggests checking that your words and actions truly match.

career.up: Your skills and resources are enough to begin. The Magician leans towards focusing on one clear aim and acting on it with intent. A pitch, a launch or a negotiation may go well when you prepare. For money, it suggests using what you have wisely.
career.rev: Reversed, the Magician suggests scattered effort, unused talent or promising more than you can deliver. Choose one task and finish it. Be honest about what you can do, and be wary of any money scheme that relies on clever talk.

feelings.up: The other person may be actively interested and willing to take the first step. They seem focused, confident and eager to impress you, perhaps with real effort. Their feelings lean towards purposeful rather than passive.
feelings.rev: The other person may be saying what you want to hear without full sincerity, or holding their feelings back behind a front. It could also be that they simply have not decided what to do. Watch whether actions follow words.

yesno.up: Yes. The Magician suggests you have the tools and the focus to make it happen. It leans towards acting with clear intent rather than waiting.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, the Magician points to scattered energy or tricks without follow-through. The answer may depend on whether you can focus and be honest about it.

advice.up: Gather your tools, pick one aim, and act on it today. Use your skills openly and keep your word. You probably have more to work with than you think.
advice.rev: Gather your attention before you start more things. Finish one thing, tell the truth about what you can offer, and use a talent you have been keeping private.

love.up: The High Priestess suggests that what is unspoken between two people matters more than what is said. In a relationship, it points to listening and quiet closeness. If single, it leans towards patience and trusting your sense of who feels right.
love.rev: Reversed, the High Priestess points to feelings kept hidden, even from yourself, or to reading too much into small signs. In a relationship, it suggests gently naming what you have not said. Single, quiet the noise and notice what you actually feel.

career.up: Stillness before a decision serves you. The High Priestess leans towards watching, listening and gathering information before you commit. Study and research go well. For money, it suggests waiting until you understand the whole picture.
career.rev: Reversed, busyness may be drowning out your inner voice, or you may be sitting on information too long. Make time to think quietly, then act. Be careful about overanalysing; not every small sign carries meaning.

feelings.up: The other person may feel a lot and say little. Their interest seems deep, private and cautious, shown through attention rather than words. They may be waiting to see whether it is safe to speak.
feelings.rev: The other person may be hiding their feelings, or unsure what they are. Mixed signals could come from secrecy rather than disinterest. It suggests asking kindly rather than guessing from small clues.

yesno.up: Maybe. The High Priestess asks for stillness first. The answer is not fully spoken yet, so listen to what you sense beneath the surface.
yesno.rev: Not yet. Reversed, she suggests you are not hearing your own answer, or that something is still hidden. Wait until the noise settles.

advice.up: Be still and listen. Sit with the question before you act, and trust what you sense before you can explain it. Keep some things private until you are sure.
advice.rev: Turn down the noise and ask what you already know. Name a feeling you have hidden, and avoid reading too much into small signs.

love.up: The Empress suggests warmth, affection and enjoyment of one another. In a relationship, it leans towards tenderness, shared meals and tending what you have built. If single, it points to nurturing yourself and the friendships around you; love grows where it is cared for.
love.rev: Reversed, the Empress points to smothering, over-giving or neglecting your own needs. In a relationship, it suggests checking whether care flows both ways. Single, it asks you to be as kind to yourself as you are to others.

career.up: Creative work and steady care are favoured. The Empress leans towards growth that comes from patient tending: a project, a team, a skill. For money, it suggests comfortable abundance built gradually, enjoyed without excess.
career.rev: Reversed, a creative dry spell, overwork or caring for everyone but yourself may be at play. Rest and feed your imagination. For money, watch overspending as comfort and neglecting your own security.

feelings.up: The other person may feel warm, generous and protective towards you. Their feelings seem affectionate and sensual, with a wish to care for you and enjoy time together. It leans towards comfort rather than drama.
feelings.rev: The other person may be giving too much, or becoming possessive, or perhaps withdrawing care because they feel drained. Their feelings could be real but tangled up with their own needs.

yesno.up: Yes. The Empress leans towards growth when you tend it well. Care, patience and enjoyment support this.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, she suggests care is blocked or overdone. Look at whether your own needs are being met before you decide.

advice.up: Tend what you love and let yourself enjoy it. Cook, make, plant or rest. Generosity works best when you include yourself.
advice.rev: Put your own needs back on the list. If you are over-giving, step back; if you feel creatively stuck, go outside and rest your mind.

love.up: The Emperor suggests steadiness, commitment and clear boundaries. In a relationship, it leans towards reliability and agreeing how you will look after each other. If single, it points to knowing what you want and standing by your standards.
love.rev: Reversed, the Emperor points to control, stubbornness or an absence of boundaries. In a relationship, it suggests asking where firmness has turned into rigidity. Single, you may be too guarded, or too willing to bend.

career.up: Structure and leadership serve you well. The Emperor leans towards planning, setting clear limits and taking responsibility. Authority figures and systems matter here. For money, it suggests budgets, savings habits and steady foundations.
career.rev: Reversed, rigid rules, an overbearing boss or a lack of any plan may be the issue. Look at where you control too tightly or where there is no structure. Flexibility with some limits can help.

feelings.up: The other person may feel protective, serious and committed, showing care through reliability rather than words. Their feelings seem steady and responsible, though perhaps reserved. They want to build something lasting.
feelings.rev: The other person may be controlling, emotionally closed or uneasy with the weight of responsibility. Their feelings could be real but expressed through rules and distance. It suggests clear, calm talk.

yesno.up: Yes. The Emperor leans towards a plan with clear structure and firm footing. Set your terms and proceed steadily.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, he points to rigidity or missing structure. The answer may depend on loosening control or building a proper plan.

advice.up: Make a plan, set clear boundaries and take responsibility. Lead calmly. Order is useful when it protects what matters to you.
advice.rev: Check where firmness has become stubbornness, or where you have no plan at all. Loosen your grip a little, or build the structure that is missing.

love.up: The Hierophant suggests commitment, shared values and the support of a community. In a relationship, it leans towards rituals, family ties and deepening trust. If single, it points to meeting someone through shared circles and valuing common ground.
love.rev: Reversed, the Hierophant points to questioning expectations about how a relationship should look. It suggests finding your own way, whether that means breaking from convention or from family pressure. Single, you may resist labels or a set script.

career.up: Learning the established way first serves you. The Hierophant leans towards mentors, formal training, qualifications and respect for proven methods. A team or institution may support you. For money, it suggests conventional, trusted routes.
career.rev: Reversed, rules that no longer fit may feel stifling, or you may refuse advice you need. Ask which conventions still help and which are just habit. Be careful of dogma at work and of blindly following others on money.

feelings.up: The other person may feel respectful, sincere and serious about you, wanting a proper, committed path. Their feelings lean towards loyalty and shared values rather than a passing thing. They may care what family and friends think.
feelings.rev: The other person may feel pulled between what they are expected to do and what they want. Their feelings could be real but held back by convention, or they may reject the usual path altogether.

yesno.up: Yes. The Hierophant leans towards what is well established, trusted and supported by others. Guidance is available if you ask.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, he suggests the usual route may not fit. Think about whether you are following a rule or your own values.

advice.up: Learn from someone who has walked this path. Join the group, honour the tradition that fits, and commit to the basics before you change them.
advice.rev: Question the rule that no longer fits, then find your own way to meaning. Stay open to learning from others even if you reject the form.

love.up: The Lovers suggests a bond that asks for honesty and a choice made from your values. In a relationship, it leans towards deeper commitment and open talk. If single, it points to a meaningful connection, or to choosing what you truly want over pleasing someone.
love.rev: Reversed, the Lovers points to misalignment, drifting apart or putting off a decision. In a relationship, it suggests checking whether your actions match what you value. Single, you may be torn or choosing to please others.

career.up: A meaningful choice at work reflects your values. The Lovers leans towards partnerships and collaborations that suit you, and towards picking the path that feels aligned. For money, it suggests choosing in line with what you believe matters.
career.rev: Reversed, indecision or mismatched values may be holding you back. A partnership may be out of tune. Ask which option you would choose if nobody was watching, and avoid leaning too hard on another person's view.

feelings.up: The other person may feel a real pull and a wish for honest connection. Their feelings seem sincere, warm and aimed at commitment, with attraction and values lining up. They may be weighing a meaningful choice about you.
feelings.rev: The other person may be unsure, torn between options, or feeling a distance growing. Their feelings could be real but not matched by action. It suggests an honest talk about what each of you wants.

yesno.up: Yes. The Lovers leans towards a choice that fits your values and a connection that is honest. Choose what you can stand behind.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, the Lovers points to a choice delayed or values out of tune. The answer may wait until you are honest with yourself.

advice.up: Choose in line with your values and tell the truth about what you want. Let a connection be honest and mutual rather than a performance.
advice.rev: Stop putting off the decision. Check whether your actions match what you say you value, and speak openly with the person involved.

love.up: The Chariot suggests driving towards what you want in love, with focus and steadiness. In a relationship, it leans towards a shared direction and working through competing pulls together. If single, it points to taking active steps and not waiting.
love.rev: Reversed, the Chariot points to pulling in different directions, forcing things or feeling stuck without a plan. In a relationship, it suggests slowing down and agreeing where you are heading. Single, you may be rushing or standing still.

career.up: Determination and discipline move you forward. The Chariot leans towards a clear goal, momentum and keeping competing demands in line. Exams, competitions and travel for work may feature. For money, it suggests focused, steady effort.
career.rev: Reversed, drive may be scattered, stalled or pushed too hard. Pause to choose a direction before you speed up. Watch that ambition does not run over colleagues, and avoid forcing a money decision.

feelings.up: The other person may feel determined to win you or to move things forward. Their feelings seem strong and purposeful, with confidence in showing them. They may be keen to take charge.
feelings.rev: The other person may be pulled two ways, unsure of direction, or pushing too hard and too fast. Their feelings might be real but turned into pressure or control. It suggests asking for space and clarity.

yesno.up: Yes. The Chariot leans towards forward movement when you hold your focus. Keep the reins steady and keep going.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, it points to scattered drive or force without direction. The answer may depend on choosing a clear course first.

advice.up: Pick a direction and commit to it. Hold your competing pulls in line with discipline, and keep moving at a steady pace.
advice.rev: Stop and ask where you are heading. Ease off the force, resolve the two-way pull inside you, and then move again.

love.up: Strength suggests patience, tenderness and quiet courage in love. In a relationship, it leans towards meeting difficult feelings with kindness rather than a fight. If single, it points to self-compassion and the confidence to be gentle and open.
love.rev: Reversed, Strength points to self-doubt, burnout or trying to tame a feeling by force. In a relationship, it suggests rest and honest sharing of your limits. Single, be kind to yourself and rebuild confidence in small steps.

career.up: Calm resilience handles what force cannot. Strength leans towards patience with a difficult colleague or task and steady confidence. Persistence pays off here. For money, it suggests staying composed and not acting from fear.
career.rev: Reversed, you may be running on empty, doubting yourself or pushing through by sheer will. Rest, ask for support and rebuild with small wins. Be careful of forcing results or acting from anxiety around money.

feelings.up: The other person may feel gentle, loyal and patient with you. Their feelings seem steady and compassionate, shown through kindness and calm support rather than grand gestures. They may admire your courage.
feelings.rev: The other person may feel insecure, drained or unable to show how much they care. Their feelings might be present but buried under self-doubt or tension. Patience and gentleness from you may help.

yesno.up: Yes. Strength leans towards success through patience and gentle persistence. You can do this without a fight.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, it points to low energy or self-doubt. The answer may depend on rest and rebuilding confidence first.

advice.up: Meet the difficulty calmly and kindly. Be patient with yourself and with others, and let courage be quiet rather than loud.
advice.rev: Rest and rebuild your confidence in small steps. Do not try to force a feeling away; give it space and speak to yourself kindly.

love.up: The Hermit suggests that time apart can clarify what you want. In a relationship, it leans towards quiet, honest reflection and perhaps some space. If single, it points to enjoying your own company and waiting for a connection that feels true.
love.rev: Reversed, the Hermit points to withdrawing too far or being unable to sit alone with yourself. In a relationship, it suggests reaching out before distance hardens. Single, balance solitude with warm company.

career.up: Stepping back to think serves you. The Hermit leans towards focused study, research or work done alone, and towards a mentor's guidance. For money, it suggests reviewing your situation quietly before you decide.
career.rev: Reversed, isolation or restlessness may be getting in the way. Do not cut yourself off from help, and do not avoid the question you need to face. Reconnect with a trusted colleague, then return to your plan.

feelings.up: The other person may feel reflective and serious, taking time to understand their feelings before sharing them. They seem thoughtful and sincere, though quiet. They may need space, which is not the same as disinterest.
feelings.rev: The other person may be withdrawing, avoiding the subject or unable to settle with their own thoughts. Their feelings might be real but hidden behind distance. They may be slowly coming back towards people.

yesno.up: Maybe. The Hermit asks you to step back and think. The answer lies in your own quiet judgement, not outside noise.
yesno.rev: Not yet. Reversed, it suggests you are avoiding the question or withdrawing too far. Reconnect, then think again.

advice.up: Take time alone to think. Turn down outside voices, light your own lamp and decide what matters to you.
advice.rev: Do not retreat further. Reach out to someone you trust, and if you cannot be still, notice what you are avoiding.

love.up: The Wheel suggests that things are turning, and love may be entering a new chapter. In a relationship, it leans towards change you can meet together. If single, it points to timing shifting in your favour, or an unexpected meeting.
love.rev: Reversed, the Wheel points to a repeating pattern or resisting a change. In a relationship, it suggests naming the loop you keep re-entering. Single, you may feel stuck, but a cycle is winding down.

career.up: Circumstances shift, and a new chapter may open. The Wheel leans towards adapting well to change and using good timing. For money, it suggests that things fluctuate, so stay flexible and keep perspective.
career.rev: Reversed, you may feel stuck in a loop or resisting a change that is already under way. Look at what you can influence and let go of what you cannot. Avoid rash money moves based on a hunch about luck.

feelings.up: The other person may feel that something is shifting and be open to change with you. Their feelings seem to be moving in a good direction, helped by timing. They may sense this as fated or fortunate.
feelings.rev: The other person may be going through a change of their own, or repeating an old pattern. Their feelings might be in flux, hard to read right now. Give it time and watch what remains steady.

yesno.up: Yes. The Wheel leans towards a favourable turn and good timing. Be ready to adapt as things move.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, the Wheel points to delays or a repeating loop. The timing may not be right yet.

advice.up: Accept that cycles turn and ride this one with an open mind. Look for what the change offers, and make the most of good timing.
advice.rev: Notice the pattern you keep repeating and choose one thing within your control. Let a winding-down cycle end rather than resisting it.

love.up: Justice suggests honesty, fairness and clear agreements in love. In a relationship, it leans towards balanced give and take, and owning your part in things. If single, it points to being truthful about what you want and what you can offer.
love.rev: Reversed, Justice points to unfairness, blame or avoiding responsibility. In a relationship, it suggests checking whether the scales are tipped, including against yourself. Single, be careful of harsh judgement of others or yourself.

career.up: Fair dealing and honest facts favour you. Justice leans towards contracts, evaluations and decisions made on the evidence. Accountability is rewarded. For money, it suggests reading the details and keeping accurate records.
career.rev: Reversed, bias, dodged responsibility or an unfair process may be at play. Review the facts again and own your share. Be careful of harsh judgement, and check any agreement carefully before relying on it.

feelings.up: The other person may feel that they want things to be honest and fair between you. Their feelings seem considered, sincere and based on a clear view of the situation. They may value truth over comfort.
feelings.rev: The other person may be avoiding responsibility, judging harshly or seeing things one-sidedly. Their feelings could be real but clouded by bias or by fear of consequences. A calm, factual conversation may help.

yesno.up: Yes. Justice leans towards a fair outcome when you look at the facts honestly. Weigh them clearly and own your part.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, bias or avoided responsibility may cloud things. The answer depends on seeing the situation fairly.

advice.up: Weigh the facts honestly, including your own role. Make fair choices, keep your word and accept the consequences.
advice.rev: Look for bias, in others and in yourself. Take responsibility where it is yours and ease up on harsh self-judgement.

love.up: The Hanged Man suggests a pause that shows you something new. In a relationship, it leans towards letting go of a fixed view and seeing your partner's side. If single, it points to waiting without forcing, and viewing love from another angle.
love.rev: Reversed, the Hanged Man points to stalling or playing the martyr. In a relationship, it suggests asking whether waiting still helps either of you. Single, you may be putting life on hold for someone who is not choosing you.

career.up: A deliberate pause lets you see the problem differently. The Hanged Man leans towards delays that turn out useful, and towards new perspectives. For money, it suggests holding off on big decisions until you see more clearly.
career.rev: Reversed, the pause may have become delay, or a sacrifice that serves no one. Decide whether waiting is still wise. If you are ready to move, make a plan and act, rather than staying suspended.

feelings.up: The other person may be in a thoughtful pause, reconsidering what they want. Their feelings seem real but not yet resolved, and they may be seeing things from a new angle. They are not rushing.
feelings.rev: The other person may be stalling, undecided, or making a sacrifice they resent. Their feelings might be real but stuck. They may also be getting ready to move after a long wait.

yesno.up: Maybe. The Hanged Man suggests waiting and looking again. The answer may come once you see it differently.
yesno.rev: Not yet. Reversed, it points to stalling without purpose. Ask whether waiting still helps, then choose.

advice.up: Pause on purpose and look at the situation from the other side. Let go of the need to force it, and be patient.
advice.rev: Ask whether waiting is still useful. If it is not, stop sacrificing and decide, or let the pause end.

love.up: Death suggests an ending in love that has already begun. In a relationship, it leans towards letting an old pattern or phase finish so something truer can start. If single, it points to closing a past chapter and clearing space.
love.rev: Reversed, Death points to clinging to something that has finished, or an ending dragged out because nobody names it. In a relationship, it suggests honestly saying what is over. Single, you may be reluctant to let a past person go.

career.up: A role, habit or belief has run its course. Death leans towards clearing out the old, which may bring relief alongside grief. A change of job or direction is possible. For money, it suggests closing what no longer works.
career.rev: Reversed, you may be resisting a needed ending or only partly accepting it. Holding on may cost more than letting go. Name what is over, and take your time to adjust rather than forcing a fresh start.

feelings.up: The other person may feel that something between you has ended or changed, and be ready to move on or begin again. Their feelings seem to be in transition. It could be closure or a transformation rather than a simple goodbye.
feelings.rev: The other person may be unable to let go, or quietly knowing it is over without saying so. Their feelings may be dragging on because nobody names them. It suggests gentle honesty.

yesno.up: No. Death suggests that this chapter is closing, so the answer leans away from keeping things as they are. Something new can follow.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, an ending is being resisted or only half accepted. The answer may become clear once you let go.

advice.up: Let go of what has run its course. Mark the ending, grieve if you need to, and clear space for what comes next.
advice.rev: Name what is already finished instead of clinging to it. Take small steps towards acceptance, and be gentle with yourself.

love.up: Temperance suggests patience, balance and blending differences. In a relationship, it leans towards compromise and a calm, steady pace. If single, it points to letting love develop gradually and keeping a middle path between extremes.
love.rev: Reversed, Temperance points to imbalance, impatience or extremes. In a relationship, it suggests one of you giving or taking too much. Single, you may want results now, or struggle to find a middle way.

career.up: Measured, patient work blends opposing demands. Temperance leans towards teamwork, steady progress and moderation. Combine ideas rather than choosing sides. For money, it suggests balancing spending and saving and a steady pace.
career.rev: Reversed, overdoing it, impatience or things pulling out of balance may be a problem. Look for where you are at an extreme and aim for a calmer rhythm. Avoid hasty money decisions.

feelings.up: The other person may feel calm, kind and willing to meet you halfway. Their feelings seem steady and patient, and they may prefer a gradual, balanced pace. They are careful rather than dramatic.
feelings.rev: The other person may be impatient, going to extremes or struggling to find a middle way. Their feelings might be real but erratic, or they may be avoiding commitment. Steadiness from you may help.

yesno.up: Yes. Temperance leans towards a good result through patience and balance. Go at a steady, measured pace.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, imbalance or impatience may get in the way. The answer may depend on moderating things.

advice.up: Blend opposing needs patiently. Take measured steps, aim for the middle path and let things combine over time.
advice.rev: Find where you are out of balance and ease it. Slow down, avoid extremes and stop expecting instant results.

love.up: The Devil suggests noticing what holds you in love: an attachment, a pattern or a fear. In a relationship, it leans towards honest talk about dependency or habit. If single, it points to naming desires without shame and seeing how much choice you really have.
love.rev: Reversed, the Devil points to a hold loosening, or to denial. In a relationship, it suggests slowly breaking an unhelpful pattern. Single, you may be quietly aware of what binds you and not yet ready to act.

career.up: You may be tied to a job, habit or belief more tightly than you need to be. The Devil leans towards honest reckoning with what keeps you there, such as money, status or fear. Naming it is the first step towards choice.
career.rev: Reversed, you may be slipping out of an old grip, or avoiding seeing it. Notice small chains you could loosen. For money, be honest about habits and debts, and seek professional support if you need it.

feelings.up: The other person may feel a strong attraction or attachment that is hard to resist. Their feelings seem intense, perhaps tangled up with habit or fear. It could be passion, or it could be a hold they do not fully choose.
feelings.rev: The other person may be stepping back from an unhealthy pull, or in denial about it. Their feelings might be loosening, or quietly questioned. They may be aware but not yet acting.

yesno.up: No. The Devil leans towards caution, as something may hold you more than you admit. Look at your real choices first.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, a hold is loosening. The answer may improve as you see clearly and act.

advice.up: Name the habit, attachment or fear that holds you. See how loosely the chains hang, and choose honestly. Support from others can help.
advice.rev: Awareness is the first step. Take one small action to loosen the grip, and be honest about what you have been avoiding.

love.up: The Tower suggests a sudden shake-up that reveals what was not stable. In a relationship, it leans towards a hard truth coming out and a chance to rebuild more honestly. If single, it points to an old illusion falling and clearing ground.
love.rev: Reversed, the Tower points to avoiding a truth or living in the aftermath of one. In a relationship, it suggests facing a slow-burning problem rather than waiting. Single, you may be quietly recovering from a private crisis.

career.up: Something built on shaky ground may come down, such as a plan, role or structure. The Tower leans towards a sudden change that, though unsettling, clears space for something more honest. For money, it suggests preparing for surprises.
career.rev: Reversed, you may be resisting something already coming apart, or watching a slow unravelling. Face it rather than wait. Take stock of what remains standing and build from there at a sensible pace.

feelings.up: The other person may be going through an upheaval, or a sudden realisation about you or themselves. Their feelings could swing sharply, with truths coming out. It suggests honesty and patience while the dust settles.
feelings.rev: The other person may be avoiding a shock, or recovering from one. Their feelings might be guarded or in turmoil. A private crisis could be affecting how they behave towards you.

yesno.up: No. The Tower suggests that the current plan is on shaky ground. Expect disruption, and consider what would be more solid.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Reversed, the worst may be passing, or a problem is slowly emerging. Face the facts before you decide.

advice.up: Let what is false fall. Stay safe, be honest, and use the clear ground to build something more solid.
advice.rev: Do not wait for the problem to grow. Face it now, take stock of what is still standing, and move gently through the aftermath.

love.up: The Star suggests gentle hope and healing after a hard stretch. In a relationship, it leans towards honest, tender closeness and renewed trust. If single, it points to being open and kind to yourself, and to quiet optimism about love.
love.rev: Reversed, the Star points to dimming hope or doubt. In a relationship, it suggests feeling detached or discouraged, and needing small acts of care. Single, keep small hopes alive without forcing anything.

career.up: Recovery and renewal are favoured. The Star leans towards slowly regaining confidence after a difficult period, with inspiration and clear purpose. For money, it suggests steady, modest progress and trust in a gradual recovery.
career.rev: Reversed, low motivation or doubt may be in the way. Be kind to yourself, rest, and take small, concrete steps rather than waiting for a sign. Avoid wishing without acting, and keep money expectations realistic.

feelings.up: The other person may feel hopeful, sincere and gently drawn to you. Their feelings seem honest, calm and healing, perhaps after a hard time. They may see something good in you and in the future.
feelings.rev: The other person may be feeling discouraged, detached or unsure of the future. Their feelings might be real but dimmed by doubt. They may need patience and small reassurance rather than big promises.

love.up: You have set something in motion and now watch the horizon for what returns. In a relationship, it points to growth and looking ahead together, perhaps a longer-distance plan. If you are single, a connection may come from further afield. Be patient and keep your outlook wide.

love.up: An opening of the heart, with a cup overflowing with water. In a relationship, it suggests renewed tenderness, a deeper bond or a new beginning. If you are single, it points to a heartfelt new connection. Welcome kindness, including towards yourself.
love.rev: Feelings are held in, blocked or poured out unseen. In a relationship, emotions may go unspoken or unreceived. If you are single, old hurt may keep your heart closed. Allow yourself to feel, gently.

career.up: A new emotional beginning in your work: creativity, fulfilment or a role that matters to you. Work and study lean towards meaningful, compassionate or creative paths. Money questions lean towards offers that feel right as well as practical. Follow what moves you.
career.rev: Creativity or enthusiasm for work is blocked or unacknowledged. Work or study may feel emotionally empty. Money decisions made from numbness need a second look. Listen to what you actually care about.

feelings.up: They feel an opening of the heart towards you, with warmth, compassion and affection. The feeling is new and sincere. They may be ready to express it.
feelings.rev: They hold their feelings back or do not know how to express them. Their emotions may be blocked or overwhelming. They may need time to open up.

yesno.up: Yes. Love, compassion and a new emotional start are offered. Accept what flows to you.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Feelings are blocked or unacknowledged. Listen to your own heart before answering.

advice.up: Open your heart to what is being offered. Let kindness flow in and out.
advice.rev: Notice what you are holding back. Allow your feelings to be seen, gently and without rush.

love.up: A meeting of equals, with two people exchanging cups under the caduceus. In a relationship, it suggests mutual respect, honesty and shared feeling. If you are single, a balanced, reciprocal connection may appear. Cherish a bond where both give and receive.
love.rev: Imbalance, miscommunication or a bond drifting apart. In a relationship, one person may give more than the other, or words are misunderstood. If you are single, you may idealise someone who has not shown the same care. Talk plainly about what each of you needs.

career.up: A partnership built on mutual respect, such as a collaboration, a deal or a good working relationship. Work, study and money lean towards agreements that work for both sides. Teamwork thrives where trust is shared. Seek fairness.
career.rev: A partnership is uneven or communication falters. Work or study may involve misunderstandings or a collaboration that drifts. Money agreements need clearer terms. Clarify expectations on both sides.

feelings.up: They feel a real connection and respect for you, wanting an equal bond. Their feelings are mutual and sincere. They are open to sharing and listening.
feelings.rev: Their feelings are unequal, or confusion makes them pull back. They may not see the connection as you do. Talk to find out where they are.

yesno.up: Yes. A balanced, mutual bond supports your question. Mutual agreement is likely.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Imbalance or miscommunication clouds the answer. Clear things up before you decide.

advice.up: Meet the other person as an equal. Listen, share honestly and build trust.
advice.rev: Address the imbalance directly. Say what you need and listen to what they need.

love.up: Joy shared with friends, three figures raising their cups. In a relationship, it suggests happy social times and friends who support you as a couple. If you are single, connections often come through friendship and community. Celebrate together.
love.rev: Overindulgence, gossip or feeling left out. In a relationship, social life may crowd the closeness, or a third person causes tension. If you are single, loneliness may show up at gatherings. Seek a few real friends rather than a big crowd.

career.up: Teamwork and shared celebration. Work, study and money lean towards collaboration, group success and a friendly workplace. The raised cups suggest mutual support and joy in shared effort. Celebrate wins together.
career.rev: Cliques, gossip or too much partying may distract from work. Work or study may feel isolating or the team turns sour. Money may be spent too freely on socialising. Keep a healthy balance.

feelings.up: They feel friendly warmth and enjoy your company. Their feelings may start in friendship and shared fun. They value the community you share.
feelings.rev: Their interest is more social than romantic, or they feel left out. They may be distracted by others. The mood may be indulgent more than intimate.

yesno.up: Yes. Joy, friendship and support from others favour you. Celebrate and share the plan.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Gossip, excess or isolation may cloud the answer. Check who truly supports you.

advice.up: Spend time with people who lift you up. Share your happiness and accept their help.
advice.rev: Step back from gossip and excess. Look for real company over a loud crowd.

love.up: You sit under a tree, arms folded, unaware of the cup being offered. In a relationship, it suggests boredom, withdrawal or missing small gestures of love. If you are single, you may be turning away from opportunities. Ask what you truly want.
love.rev: You wake up to something you ignored. In a relationship, interest returns and you notice what was offered. If you are single, you open to new invitations after a dull patch. Or you may sink further into apathy if you do not act.

career.up: Boredom or apathy at work or study makes you overlook what is on offer. The cloud-offered cup suggests an unnoticed opportunity. Money questions lean towards reviewing options. Pause, reflect and ask what truly interests you.
career.rev: You notice an opportunity you dismissed and are ready to engage. Work or study may revive after a flat period. Money options deserve another look. Take action on what you now see.

feelings.up: They feel bored, withdrawn or unsure what they want. Their feelings may be turned inward, and they may overlook what you offer. They need time to reflect.
feelings.rev: They wake up to their feelings or to what you offer. Interest may return after a distant spell. They may also remain stuck if nothing changes.

yesno.up: Maybe. You may be missing what is offered, and the answer is not clear. Reflect before you decide.
yesno.rev: Yes. You see the offer you ignored and are ready to accept it. Act on it.

advice.up: Take time to reflect, but look up. Check whether boredom is hiding an offer.
advice.rev: Take hold of the cup you have noticed. Move from reflection to action.

love.up: Grief and regret over spilled cups, while two still stand behind. In a relationship, it suggests mourning a loss or a rift, and focusing on what went wrong. If you are single, past heartbreak may colour how you see the present. Allow the grief, then turn around.
love.rev: You begin to move on, forgive and turn towards what remains. In a relationship, healing and reconciliation are possible. If you are single, recovery from loss opens a little room for new love. Be kind to yourself as you turn.

career.up: Disappointment over a loss or failure at work, study or money. The black cloak and spilled cups suggest regret, while the standing cups point to what is left. Dwell for a moment, then assess what remains. Look for the cups still full.
career.rev: You recover from a setback and begin to see options again. Work or study improves as you let go of regret. Money matters recover slowly. Move forward with what you have learned.

feelings.up: They feel sadness, regret or disappointment, perhaps about the relationship. Their feelings are tied to loss, and they find it hard to see what remains. They may need comfort.
feelings.rev: They begin to heal and let go of resentment. Their feelings turn towards what is still good. They may be open to a fresh start.

yesno.up: No. Loss and regret colour this moment, so the answer is not favourable now. Remember that some cups still stand.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Healing has started and a better answer may come. Move on gently.

advice.up: Let yourself grieve, then look at the two cups still standing. Don't stay in blame.
advice.rev: Forgive where you can, and slowly turn to what remains. Healing takes time.

love.up: Warm memories and gentle generosity, with children offering flowers in a cup. In a relationship, it suggests old affection, shared history or simple kindness. If you are single, someone from your past or a familiar, comforting person may return. Treasure the sweetness without living in it.
love.rev: Stuck in the past, or looking back instead of ahead. In a relationship, nostalgia can hide present problems, or old issues resurface. If you are single, an ex or old ideal may block new love. Let the past be a memory.

career.up: Familiar surroundings, old colleagues or a return to earlier work or study. Money questions lean towards simple generosity, gifts or inheritance from the past. The card suggests kindness and warmth in your environment. Draw on what you learned before.
career.rev: You cling to old ways and avoid change. Work or study may hold you in what is comfortable but outdated. Money habits from the past may need updating. Honour memories, then move forward.

feelings.up: They feel fondness, nostalgia and tenderness towards you. Their feelings may be rooted in shared history or sweet memories. They are gentle and kind.
feelings.rev: They are caught in the past or comparing you to someone from it. Their feelings may rely too much on memory. They may need to let go of what was.

yesno.up: Yes. Warmth, memory and kindness favour you. Look to what has worked before.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The past may be holding you back, so look forward before you decide.

advice.up: Revisit happy memories and act with simple kindness. Reconnect with someone from your past if it feels right.
advice.rev: Do not live in yesterday. Let the memories rest and look at what is in front of you.

love.up: Many dreams float in clouds, each cup holding a different promise. In a relationship, it suggests idealising or imagining more than is there. If you are single, you may have many options but no clear choice. Sort fantasy from what is real.
love.rev: Clarity arrives, or choices overwhelm. In a relationship, illusions fade and you see things as they are. If you are single, you may finally choose one thing, or feel lost in options. Focus on what you truly want.

career.up: A wealth of options and daydreams, calling for clear sorting. Work, study and money lean towards many ideas and little commitment. The shrouded figure faces cups of treasure, jewels and a dragon, hinting at illusion. Choose one realistic plan.
career.rev: The fog clears and you see which options are real. Work or study may focus once you stop daydreaming. Money choices improve with clearer facts. Or you may be lost in fantasy and decide nothing.

feelings.up: They have many feelings and fantasies, and may not know what they want. Their interest may be more imaginary than real. They may be unclear about you.
feelings.rev: They see things more clearly, or are overwhelmed by options. Their illusions about you are fading. They may finally decide what they want.

yesno.up: Maybe. Many possibilities and some illusion cloud the answer. Sort the real from the imagined first.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The fog is lifting, but you must still choose. Check facts before you decide.

advice.up: Write down your options and test which ones are real. Pick one and take a step.
advice.rev: Clear the fog. Face the facts and make a decision, rather than drifting in daydreams.

love.up: Walking away from something that looks fine but no longer satisfies. In a relationship, it suggests leaving, or an emotional distance that is growing. If you are single, you may be leaving a pattern that did not nourish you. Seek what you truly need.
love.rev: Staying out of fear, or leaving without a plan. In a relationship, you may linger in a hollow bond, or leave without facing why. If you are single, aimless drifting may delay real connection. Be honest about what you want.

career.up: You leave a stack of cups behind and head for the mountains under the moon. Work, study and money lean towards leaving a role that no longer fits, in search of meaning. It takes courage to walk away from the comfortable. Plan the journey.
career.rev: You stay in an unfulfilling job out of fear, or leave in a rush. Work or study may stall in aimless drifting. Money risks need a plan. Decide whether to stay or go with open eyes.

feelings.up: They are drawn to leave or withdraw, searching for something more. Their feelings may have cooled or they feel unfulfilled. They may be walking away, even if it is hard.
feelings.rev: They linger out of fear, or leave without saying why. Their feelings are mixed and unspoken. They may hesitate between staying and going.

yesno.up: Maybe. Walking away may serve you, but it is not an easy yes. Ask what is truly missing.
yesno.rev: No. Fear or drifting makes the move unwise as it stands. Make a plan or face why you are stuck.

advice.up: Be honest about what no longer fills you. Leave with care and carry the lessons.
advice.rev: Don't run, and don't hide. Face why you want to go, then choose to stay or leave on purpose.

love.up: Contentment and a wish fulfilled, the figure seated before their cups. In a relationship, it suggests satisfaction, enjoyment and gratitude for each other. If you are single, you are happy in your own company, which makes you open to love. Savour what you have.
love.rev: Smugness or a wish that is not as satisfying as expected. In a relationship, dissatisfaction may hide behind a pleasant surface. If you are single, getting what you wanted may feel empty. Look at what you truly need.

career.up: Satisfaction with what you have worked for, as your cups line up behind you. Work, study and money lean towards a job well done, comfort and enjoying your results. Gratitude suits this card. Enjoy it, and share it.
career.rev: Dissatisfaction despite having what you wanted, or showing off. Work or study may fall short of the reward you imagined. Money gains may feel hollow. Ask what would truly fulfil you.

feelings.up: They feel content and happy with you. Their feelings are warm and satisfied. They enjoy the connection and are grateful for it.
feelings.rev: They feel unsatisfied even though things look fine, or are complacent. Their feelings may be shallow or smug. They may want more than they have.

yesno.up: Yes. The Nine of Cups is the wish card: contentment and satisfaction are on offer. Enjoy it.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Getting what you wanted may not feel as good as hoped. Check what you truly want.

advice.up: Appreciate what you have and enjoy it without guilt. Thank those who helped you.
advice.rev: Look beyond the surface. If satisfaction feels empty, ask what you actually want.

love.up: A picture of a happy home beneath a rainbow of cups. In a relationship, it suggests emotional fulfilment, family bonds and shared contentment. If you are single, belonging and a loving community may shape your future. Cherish the people you love.
love.rev: Strain in a family or group, or an ideal out of reach. In a relationship, values may not line up, or the picture looks better than it feels. If you are single, you may long for a perfect picture. Talk honestly about what each of you wants.

career.up: Emotional fulfilment in a team or workplace that feels like family. Work, study and money lean towards harmony, shared success and security at home. The rainbow suggests lasting reward. Seek work that matches your values.
career.rev: Tension in a team, or an ideal that hides real issues. Work or study may clash with your values or home life. Money matters may strain family harmony. Address the cracks rather than the picture.

feelings.up: They feel deep affection and may imagine a shared home or family life with you. Their feelings are warm, loyal and committed. They value belonging.
feelings.rev: Their feelings are tied to an ideal that does not fit reality. They may feel strain with family or values. Honest conversation is needed.

yesno.up: Yes. Harmony, belonging and emotional fulfilment support your question. It looks happy.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Strained bonds or an idealised picture cast doubt. Address the issues first.

advice.up: Nurture the bonds you value and share your happiness. Make your home a place of warmth.
advice.rev: Be honest about the issues behind the ideal. Work on communication and shared values.

love.up: A tender, creative message arrives, as a fish pops from the cup. In a relationship, it suggests sweet gestures, playful surprise and softness. If you are single, a gentle, imaginative person or a message of interest may appear. Listen to your feelings.
love.rev: Feelings are held back or become melodrama. In a relationship, moodiness or immaturity may cause trouble. If you are single, daydreams may stand in for real contact. Name your feelings honestly and calmly.

career.up: A creative impulse or a gentle message about work, study or money. The card suggests being open to surprise and trusting your imagination. Opportunities may come through intuition or the arts. Follow a small, heartfelt idea.
career.rev: Creative blocks, moodiness or escape into daydreams. Work or study may suffer from oversensitivity or unrealistic hopes. Money decisions are best made when calm. Ground your ideas.

feelings.up: They feel tender, shy and a little dreamy about you. Their feelings may arrive as a small gift, message or kind gesture. They are sincere, if still learning how to say it.
feelings.rev: They hold back or feel moody about their feelings. Their interest may be mixed with daydreams or immaturity. They may need time to grow up emotionally.

yesno.up: Yes. A gentle, hopeful message supports your question. Trust your feelings.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Moodiness or unclear feelings blur the answer. Wait until you feel calm.

advice.up: Follow your gentle impulses and be creative. Listen to what your feelings tell you.
advice.rev: Don't let moods run you. Ground your dreams with one practical step.

love.up: A romantic, charming figure on a calm horse, offering a cup. In a relationship, it suggests romance, an invitation or a gesture of devotion. If you are single, a dreamy, courteous person may approach. Enjoy the romance, and check it is real.
love.rev: Charm without substance, or a retreat from feeling. In a relationship, promises may outrun reality, or someone pulls away. If you are single, mixed signals or an idealised crush may mislead you. Look for consistency.

career.up: An offer or invitation arrives that moves you. Work, study and money lean towards creative, idealistic paths and pursuing what you care about. The Knight carries his cup with care. Weigh the offer against practical needs.
career.rev: Unrealistic ideas or mixed signals. Work or study may suffer from daydreaming or unkept promises. Money offers need checking. Look past the charm to the details.

feelings.up: They feel romantic and idealistic about you, and may offer a heartfelt gesture. Their feelings are sincere, though perhaps dreamy. They may be courting you in their own gentle style.
feelings.rev: Their charm is stronger than their commitment, or they retreat from feeling. Their promises may outrun reality. Their intentions may be unclear.

yesno.up: Yes. An offer or romantic gesture supports your question. Follow your heart with open eyes.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Mixed signals or unrealistic hopes cast doubt. Check what is real.

advice.up: Follow your heart and accept the invitation, with your feet still on the ground.
advice.rev: Don't be swept off by charm alone. Ask for consistent actions, not just words.

love.up: Deep feeling held with care, the Queen gazing at an ornate cup. In a relationship, it suggests empathy, devotion and intuitive understanding. If you are single, a caring, sensitive connection may come. Look after your own heart as well.
love.rev: Empathy tips into over-giving, or feelings are shut away. In a relationship, one of you may absorb the other's moods or lose boundaries. If you are single, you may protect yourself too much. Care for yourself as well as others.

career.up: Empathy and intuition guide your work, study and money choices. Caring professions, creative or counselling roles may suit. The Queen sits at the water's edge, suggesting emotional depth. Trust your instincts, with sensible limits.
career.rev: Emotional overwhelm or neglecting your own needs. Work or study may drain you as you take on others' feelings. Money decisions made from sympathy may need care. Set boundaries.

feelings.up: They feel deep care, empathy and affection towards you. Their feelings are gentle, intuitive and sincere. They want to understand and support you.
feelings.rev: They feel overwhelmed or hold back to protect themselves. Their care may turn into over-giving, or they shut down. They need space to look after themselves.

yesno.up: Yes. Compassion and intuition support you. Trust your inner sense.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Emotional overwhelm clouds your judgement. Care for your own needs first.

advice.up: Trust your intuition and care for others, including yourself. Be gentle but keep your boundaries.
advice.rev: Stop over-giving. Step back, rest and attend to your own feelings.

love.up: Mature, steady love: calm, kind and emotionally balanced. In a relationship, it suggests patience, diplomacy and a partner who can hold feeling without being ruled by it. If you are single, a thoughtful, grounded person may appear. Seek calm over drama.
love.rev: Suppressed feelings or moodiness hiding behind composure. In a relationship, emotional distance or subtle manipulation may creep in. If you are single, you may guard your heart too tightly. Let some feeling show.

career.up: Emotional maturity guides your work, study and money matters. Diplomacy, advice and steady leadership suit this card. The King sits on a throne on rough water, calm among motion. Keep your head and be compassionate.
career.rev: Control of feeling hardens into coldness, or composure cracks. Work or study may involve suppressed stress or moodiness. Money decisions may be made from avoidance. Admit what you feel.

feelings.up: They feel steady, caring affection, and respond with maturity. Their feelings are deep but measured, and they are reliable. They show love through calm support.
feelings.rev: They hide feelings behind composure or keep their distance. Their emotions may be suppressed or confusing. They may struggle to open up.

yesno.up: Yes. Emotional balance and calm judgement favour your question. Move forward with care.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Suppressed feelings or moodiness cloud the answer. Be honest about what you feel.

advice.up: Stay calm under pressure and feel deeply while choosing how to respond. Offer steady care.
advice.rev: Don't bury what you feel. Let honest emotion in before it turns cold or breaks out.

love.up: In a relationship, this suggests a conversation that finally says what has gone unsaid. The sword cuts through mixed signals, so plain, kind honesty helps both of you. If you are single, it points to seeing clearly what you want before you go looking.
love.rev: Reversed, words may come out sharper than intended, or a truth stays swallowed. Partners may talk past each other. If you are single, muddled expectations could be clouding things, so name what you really want before acting.

career.up: This points to a sharp idea or a clear decision arriving in your work or studies. The crowned sword suggests a breakthrough you can act on once you state the goal plainly. Money choices also lean towards being simple and well reasoned.
career.rev: Your thinking may feel foggy, and a proposal or plan could be unclear or poorly worded. It suggests slowing down and checking facts before you commit. Avoid sending sharp messages to colleagues when you are frustrated.

feelings.up: This person sees you clearly and wants honesty between you. Their feelings tend to be direct rather than coy, and they may be ready to say where they stand. They value truth and a clean start.
feelings.rev: This person may be confused about how they feel, or holding back something they know. Their words may come out harsh or not at all. The picture is unclear until someone speaks plainly.

yesno.up: Yes. The raised sword and its crown point to clarity and a decisive step. If the question is plain and you have the facts, the answer leans towards a clear go-ahead.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The cloud is thick here, so the facts are not yet clear or something is being avoided. Clarify the question before relying on any answer.

advice.up: Think it through, then say it simply. Write down the one idea that matters and act on it, using words that are honest but not cutting.
advice.rev: Pause before you speak or decide. Ask what you are avoiding admitting, and give yourself time to untangle your thoughts before taking them to others.

love.up: A relationship may be at a stalemate, with both of you guarding your hearts behind crossed swords. The blindfold suggests something is not being looked at. Honest talk, when you are ready, can lower the swords. If single, you may be shutting out options to stay safe.
love.rev: Reversed, the blindfold slips and a hidden feeling comes to light, or the standoff drags on with no resolution. Partners may be forced to face a choice. If single, you may finally admit what you really want.

career.up: You face a choice at work or about money, and you are avoiding it by refusing to look. Equal options can feel impossible to weigh. The card suggests gathering facts, then deciding, rather than staying balanced forever.
career.rev: A decision gets forced, or new information arrives that breaks the deadlock. Alternatively the indecision drags on and costs you time. Look at the facts you have been avoiding and choose.

feelings.up: This person is guarded and unsure. They may care but are keeping their emotions behind a wall, unwilling to commit to a view. They could be torn between two feelings.
feelings.rev: This person is starting to see their own feelings more clearly, or is being pushed to decide. Alternatively they are still stuck, and silence continues. Expect some movement, but not necessarily comfort.

yesno.up: Not yet. The crossed swords and blindfold suggest the answer is on hold because a choice is being avoided. Get more information before asking again.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The blindfold is slipping, so something may soon be clear, but the deadlock may also persist. Wait for the new facts.

advice.up: Take off the blindfold when you are ready. List what you know and what you fear, then make the smallest honest choice you can.
advice.rev: Face what you have been avoiding, because it may be forced on you anyway. Gather the missing information and decide on your own terms.

love.up: In a relationship, this suggests a painful truth or a hurt that needs to be felt, perhaps betrayal or a hard conversation. Talking honestly helps more than hiding. If you are single, an old heartbreak may still be sore.
love.rev: Reversed, healing begins and the pain starts to ease, or you may be replaying an old hurt and keeping the wound open. Forgiveness, of yourself or another, may be near. If single, you are slowly opening again.

career.up: Disappointment at work or study is likely, such as a rejection, a conflict, or bad news about money. The three swords through the heart suggest it stings, but naming it is the first step. Seek support rather than carrying it alone.
career.rev: You are recovering from a setback, and the sting is fading. You may also be dwelling on past criticism or a job lost. Learn what you can from it and move on.

feelings.up: This person may feel hurt, or may be causing hurt through painful honesty. Their feelings include sorrow or disappointment. Something unsaid is weighing on them.
feelings.rev: This person is healing from hurt and may be ready to let go of old pain. Alternatively they are still holding onto a grievance. Their feelings are softening slowly.

yesno.up: No. The heart pierced by three swords suggests sorrow and a hard truth. The honest answer is likely not the one you hope for.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Pain is easing, and recovery is possible, but old wounds may still colour the answer. Allow time before expecting a clear yes.

advice.up: Let yourself feel the hurt and speak about it with someone you trust. Honesty with yourself is the first step towards healing.
advice.rev: Gently put the pain down. Forgive where you can, and notice whether you are clinging to the hurt out of habit.

love.up: In a relationship, this suggests a quiet pause. You may need rest or space, or time together without demands. If single, a break from dating to recover and recharge is wise. Retreating is healthy, as long as you do not hide for too long.
love.rev: Reversed, restlessness sets in, or one of you jumps back into emotional intensity before you are ready. If you are single, you may rush into dating while still tired. Rest a little longer.

career.up: Your work or study life asks for a pause. The resting knight on the tomb suggests recovery after strain. Step back from money worries or deadlines to recharge, and plan before you return.
career.rev: You may feel restless, or you are returning to work too soon and risking burnout. Ignoring tiredness can cost you later. Build rest into your routine.

feelings.up: This person needs space and quiet. They may be withdrawn or recovering, not rejecting you. Their feelings are still there, but they are low on energy.
feelings.rev: This person is restless or coming back into contact sooner than they should. They may feel pressure to act before they have healed. Give them room.

yesno.up: Not yet. The still figure suggests waiting and resting. The answer needs time and a calmer mind.
yesno.rev: Maybe. You are restless to act, but resting longer may still be wiser. Check you are not rushing.

advice.up: Rest on purpose. Close the door for a while, recover, and let your mind settle before the next move.
advice.rev: Do not rush back. Notice whether your restlessness is energy or avoidance, and take the remaining rest you need.

love.up: In a relationship, this suggests a quarrel where winning costs more than it gains. Pride and point-scoring can leave both people alone. If you are single, watch for old rivalries or defensive habits. Choose which arguments are worth having.
love.rev: Reversed, peace may be made, or you walk away from an argument. Alternatively, resentment lingers long after the fight. An apology could help clear the air.

career.up: Conflict at work or study is likely, with a hollow win or someone left behind. The smirking figure holds the swords while others walk away in defeat. Think about what a win actually costs, including money and goodwill.
career.rev: Tension is easing, and you may make amends or step back from a rivalry. Some resentment may linger. Repair relationships where you can.

feelings.up: This person may feel competitive or defensive with you. They could be keeping score, or feeling they lost something. Their feelings are tangled in pride.
feelings.rev: This person is ready to make peace, or wants to leave the conflict behind. They may also still be bitter. Their feelings lean towards softening.

yesno.up: No. The scattered swords and departing figures suggest a win that costs too much. Expect conflict or a hollow result.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The fight may be ending, but resentment may remain. Peace is possible if someone lets go first.

advice.up: Choose your battles. Ask whether being right is worth the cost, and walk away when the fight is not worth winning.
advice.rev: Make amends or let it go. Drop the grudge, and consider whether an honest apology would serve you better than victory.

love.up: In a relationship, this suggests moving together into calmer waters after a difficult time. The boat carries lessons with it, so some old hurt may still need care. If you are single, you are gradually leaving a painful chapter behind and healing.
love.rev: Reversed, you may resist moving on, or old baggage follows you into the new relationship. Passage may be delayed. If single, unresolved feelings for a past partner may be in the way.

career.up: Work or study moves into a calmer phase, perhaps a change of job, place or approach. The ferry crossing suggests a slow, steady passage away from trouble. Bring your lessons but leave the heaviest worries behind.
career.rev: A move is delayed or you are carrying old problems into the new situation. You may be reluctant to change. Deal with leftover issues before you go.

feelings.up: This person wants to move on from difficulty and find peace with you. Their feelings are tender and cautious, growing slowly as things calm. They are learning from the past.
feelings.rev: This person is stuck in the past, or carrying baggage into how they feel about you. They may be reluctant to move forward. Their feelings come with some unfinished business.

yesno.up: Yes. The boat is moving towards calmer water, so the answer leans towards a gentle improvement over time.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The passage is delayed or old baggage is still in the boat. Progress is possible once you deal with it.

advice.up: Let yourself move on gradually. Take your lessons, leave what you can, and trust the slow crossing.
advice.rev: Look at what you are carrying and what is holding you at the shore. Unpack the baggage so the journey can begin.

love.up: In a relationship, this suggests secrecy, avoidance or someone not being fully honest. It may also be you holding something back. If single, you might be guarding yourself or playing games. Honest conversation protects trust.
love.rev: Reversed, the truth comes out and someone comes clean, or a hidden plan is caught. This can clear the air or cause a scene. If single, you may stop hiding behind a cautious front.

career.up: Work or money calls for careful strategy, but the figure sneaking away with swords warns against cutting corners. It may signal someone taking credit or avoiding responsibility. Be honest about the cost of any shortcut.
career.rev: A scheme backfires, or you come clean about a mistake. Being caught out may happen. Taking responsibility now often costs less than hiding.

feelings.up: This person may be holding something back, or avoiding a direct conversation. Their feelings are hard to read and they may be hiding some of them. Watch how their words match their actions.
feelings.rev: This person may be ready to be honest about what they feel, or has been caught out in an evasion. The truth is surfacing. Their feelings become clearer.

yesno.up: Maybe. Sneaking off with swords suggests a clever route, but also something hidden. The outcome depends on honesty about the cost.
yesno.rev: No. The plan is likely to unravel or be discovered. A direct approach would serve you better.

advice.up: Be strategic, but do not be sly. If you take an indirect route, ask what you are not saying and who it may affect.
advice.rev: Come clean before you are found out. Take responsibility and look for a more honest way forward.

love.rev: Reversed, you slip the ropes and see choices again, perhaps finding your voice in a relationship. If single, you are letting go of limiting stories. Courage is returning.

career.up: You feel stuck in your work, study or money situation and cannot see options. The blindfold and loose bindings suggest your view is narrower than the reality. List what you can actually change.
career.rev: A way out opens as you take off the blindfold. You begin to see choices and ask for help. Act on the first small option.

feelings.up: This person feels stuck or afraid of what they feel. They may be unable to act, held back by anxiety or self-doubt. Their feelings are not absent, only bound.
feelings.rev: This person is starting to find their voice. They may be freeing themselves from fear or an old story. Their feelings become easier to express.

yesno.up: No. The bound, blindfolded figure suggests feeling trapped, so a clear yes is unlikely right now. Check whether the limits are real.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The blindfold is coming off and options reappear. The answer may improve once you see more clearly.

advice.up: Remove the blindfold. Ask what is truly stopping you, then take one small step. The ropes may be looser than they seem.
advice.rev: Keep stepping out. Trust that choices exist, and ask someone you trust to help you see them.

career.up: Worries about work, study or money keep you awake. The swords on the wall suggest the fear is louder in your head than in fact. Make a plan, share the load, and check what is truly within your control.
career.rev: Stress is easing, or you are buried under it. Seek support from colleagues, friends or professionals if it feels too heavy.

feelings.up: This person is anxious and may be lying awake over you or the situation. Their feelings include worry and guilt rather than indifference. They may fear saying the wrong thing.
feelings.rev: This person is calming down, or is buried in worry and withdrawn. Their feelings are hard to reach until the fear lifts. Offer reassurance.

yesno.up: No. The night worries suggest fear is clouding the question, so the answer leans no for now. Look again in daylight.
yesno.rev: Maybe. Fears are easing, and the picture may brighten. Ask again once you are calmer.

advice.up: Tell someone what keeps you awake. Write the worries down, and separate real problems from fears in the dark.
advice.rev: Reach out for support and do not battle alone. Remember that worry often fades by morning.

love.rev: Reversed, recovery slowly begins, or you refuse to let a painful ending go. The dawn is on the horizon. If single, you are rising from old wounds, with gentle steps.

career.up: A work, study or money chapter ends painfully, such as a loss or a final blow. The ten swords suggest it cannot get worse. Accept the ending and plan for the new start.

feelings.up: This person feels worn out or at the end of something. Their feelings may be heavy with sorrow, or finished. A fresh start is the only way for them.
feelings.rev: This person is recovering and beginning to look forward. They may also cling to hurt. Their feelings are slowly lifting.

yesno.up: No. The ten swords and the dark sky suggest an ending. The answer is no, though dawn lies behind it.
yesno.rev: Maybe. The sun is rising and recovery has begun. A yes may be possible once the old chapter is closed.

advice.up: Accept the ending. Rest, and let go of what has finished. The only direction left is forward.
advice.rev: Stop reliving the pain. Let recovery take its time, and resist the role of victim.

love.rev: Reversed, gossip, careless remarks or scattered thoughts get in the way. Partners may speak before thinking. If single, you may be overthinking or playing mind games.

career.up: Work or study favours research, questions and fresh ideas. The Page watches the sky with sword raised, suggesting vigilance and a quick mind. Gather facts and learn before you commit.
career.rev: Ideas scatter, gossip distracts, or you act in haste. Focus on one task, check your facts, and watch your words.

feelings.up: This person is curious about you and keen to learn more. Their feelings are alert and playful, driven by interest. They enjoy talking with you.
feelings.rev: This person may be gossiping or sending mixed messages. Their feelings are hard to pin down, as thoughts race. They may be using words carelessly.

yesno.rev: Maybe. Scattered thoughts or gossip cloud the picture. Check your facts before deciding.

advice.up: Ask questions and gather facts. Stay curious, and keep your words honest and kind.
advice.rev: Think before you speak. Avoid gossip, and settle on one idea before chasing the next.

feelings.up: This person is direct and passionate, but may move too quickly. Their feelings come out forcefully, and they may not listen. They want to act.

yesno.rev: No. Haste and carelessness are likely to cause trouble. Slow down before trying again.

advice.rev: Stop and check the details. Do not push on out of pride, and consider whether you are overthinking.

feelings.up: This person sees you clearly and values honesty. Their feelings may be reserved but sincere, and they say what they mean. They respect independence.
feelings.rev: This person may be cold, critical or guarded. They might be hiding feelings behind sharpness. Their feelings are not absent, only protected.

advice.rev: Soften your stance. Check that you are not using authority or logic to shut people out.

love.rev: Reversed, a chance may be missed or a relationship lacks a foundation. Partners may not be making plans. If single, you may overlook someone steady, or rush without groundwork.

feelings.rev: This person may feel the connection lacks pride or cooperation. Their feelings are lukewarm, or you are not on the same page. Talk about it.

advice.rev: Loosen your grip, and be generous without being reckless. Notice where control has become a habit.

love.rev: Reversed, warmth returns and you begin to recover, or you refuse help and stay outside. If single, you take a step towards connection.

career.rev: Recovery begins, and finances improve. Alternatively pride stops you from asking for support. Accept help where it is offered.

feelings.rev: This person is recovering and ready to let you in. Alternatively they refuse help and stay distant. Their feelings are warming slowly.

advice.rev: Accept the help on offer. Let go of pride, and take recovery one step at a time.

advice.rev: Check for strings attached. Make the exchange fairer, and give without hidden expectations.

love.rev: Reversed, impatience or doubt about progress strains things. Partners may question whether it is worth the effort. If single, you may give up on someone too early.

feelings.rev: This person is impatient or doubtful about the relationship. Their feelings are unsure, and they may be thinking of walking away. Give it time.

advice.rev: Do not quit too soon. Check whether the effort is being used well, and then go on or change course.

love.rev: Reversed, perfectionism or routine takes the joy from things. Partners may feel stuck in drudgery. If single, you may bury yourself in work to avoid dating.

career.rev: Perfectionism, burnout or shoddy work may creep in. The grind loses its purpose. Take a break and refocus on why you do it.
